title: Numeric sequences with a logical missing position become ID sequences
observed: For id=s1/s2, numeric T1/T3 and T2=NA, extraction returns id and T2. The resulting network has nodes s1 and s2; the actual states are metadata. This silently affects core estimation and every new sequence verb.
cause: The numeric position-run detector requires is.numeric() for every position. An all-missing column created with NA is logical. The analogous categorical detector allows all-missing positions, but this branch does not.
fix: Allow all-missing columns within an otherwise numeric position run, while requiring evidence of numeric positions. Until fixed, supply cols=c("T1","T2","T3").
test: Assert inferred and explicitly selected state matrices agree for numeric positions plus logical NA, with an ID column present. Check node labels as well as output dimensions.
code:
d <- data.frame(id=c('s1','s2'), T1=c(1,2), T2=NA, T3=c(2,1))
extract_sequences(d)
build_network(d, method='relative')$nodes
resolution: Numeric numbered positions now accept logical all-missing columns.

title: Post-hoc covariates determine the clusters they are tested against
status: Pre-existing at CRAN baseline; freshly reproduced
observed: Eight identical A→B sequences split perfectly into H and L groups when outcome is included in the raw frame and supplied as a post-hoc covariate. The function then reports outcomeL odds ratio 81. In this toy example the p-value is .0623; no significant result is claimed.
cause: The entire raw data frame reaches sequence encoding and distance calculation before covariates are resolved. Outcome is treated as an extra sequence position, manufacturing the clustering signal. This violates post-hoc semantics.
fix: Resolve and remove named covariates before encoding, retain them separately, and preserve alignment. A network with covariates already in metadata, or a separate covariate data frame with sequence-only input, avoids this trigger.
test: Changing a post-hoc covariate must leave the sequence distance matrix unchanged. Include constant true sequences and categorical/numeric named covariates.
code:
d <- data.frame(V1=rep('A',8), V2=rep('B',8),
                outcome=rep(c('H','L'),each=4))
f <- build_clusters(d,k=2,covariates='outcome')
f$assignments # 1 1 1 1 2 2 2 2
resolution: Requested covariates are removed before distance calculation; external frames preserve unrelated same-name positions.

title: Loading uncertainty uses strength weights for an equal-weight fit
observed: An equal-weight composite has six observed loadings of 1/3. loading_stability() returns means .40279, .40214, .19507, .39981, .39849 and .20170; all six observed weights lie outside their bootstrap intervals. With fixed equal weighting, the resampled weights should remain 1/3.
cause: Resamples call .pc_network_loadings() directly and do not replay x$meta$weighting or the weighting transformation. Confidence intervals therefore describe a different estimator. This also requires attention for eigen, factor and custom weighting.
fix: Replay the fitted weighting scheme in each resample. Preserve fixed weights for equal/custom schemes and refit only data-dependent schemes using their original settings.
test: For equal weights, assert every draw is 1/cluster_size and bootstrap SD is zero. For fitted schemes, compare a deterministic resample with an explicit full rebuild.
code:
# Full deterministic n=4000 fixture is in the evidence script.
f <- build_mcml_pc(d, clusters, aggregation='composite',
                   weighting='equal',method='cor',cor_method='pearson')
loading_stability(f,iter=30,seed=3)$summary
resolution: Fits retain the weighting specification and bootstrap draws replay it, including custom schemes and factor options. Older custom fits without a specification request a rebuild.

title: Pattern outcome overwrites a real adjustment named .outcome
status: Post-CRAN new function; incomplete name-collision protection
observed: For the same 39-row data, the pattern coefficient is .9285199 when adjusting for score. Renaming score to .outcome changes the coefficient to 8.9e-12. The function has replaced the adjustment with the outcome itself.
cause: Vector and last_obs outcomes are written into units$.outcome before adjustment/group columns are extracted. Later internal model-column renaming protects other names but occurs too late for this collision.
fix: Keep the response separately or allocate a collision-free temporary name before modifying units. This also protects a grouping column named .outcome.
test: Assert fitted coefficients are invariant when adjustment/group columns are renamed, including .outcome, for explicit vector and last_obs outcomes.
resolution: Generated responses are held separately from metadata, protecting .outcome adjustments and grouping columns.

title: Comparisons ignore node names when matrix orders differ
observed: Comparing a named matrix with a simultaneous row/column permutation of itself produces mean absolute difference 1.7777778 and Pearson .3809524, although both encode the same graph. Different named node sets of equal size are also accepted.
cause: Only dimensions are validated; subtraction and correlation use matrix positions. Reordering a correctly labelled input silently changes the result.
fix: Align equal named node sets before computing statistics, and reject incompatible named sets. Retain a documented positional fallback for unnamed inputs.
test: Compare a graph to its reordered self: all differences zero, Pearson one. Add incompatible-node and one-unnamed-input controls.
resolution: Named axes are validated and aligned; incompatible named sets are rejected. Unnamed inputs retain positional matching.

title: Gaussian confidence intervals conflict with the displayed t tests
observed: For six observations, slope .6 has SE .2390457 and p=.06605877. The displayed nominal 95% interval [.131479,1.068521] excludes zero; the ordinary linear-model t interval is [-.06369732,1.26369732].
cause: The Gaussian GLM estimates dispersion and reports Student t p-values. The effect-table code always uses qnorm() for intervals, yielding narrower intervals at small residual degrees of freedom.
fix: Use the appropriate residual-df t quantile for ordinary Gaussian fits. Treat binomial and mixed-model approximations explicitly.
test: Compare ordinary Gaussian intervals against confint(lm(...)) across residual degrees of freedom; check consistency between zero inclusion and the unadjusted two-sided test.
resolution: Ordinary Gaussian intervals use residual-df Student t quantiles, matching their displayed tests.

title: Z centrality silently underflows to zero for large hyperedges
observed: A single uniform hyperedge of 150 nodes returns every Z entry as 7.606786e-163 and an L2 norm of zero, with no warning. The symmetry solution is 1/sqrt(150)=.08164966 per node. At 400 nodes all entries are zero.
cause: The rewritten iteration squares a tiny tensor product before shifting/rescaling. Those squares underflow, and a zero norm is mistaken for an absent tensor. The earlier shift-first kernel preserves the symmetric solution on this example; that does not establish its correctness for all large graphs.
fix: Use stable normalization and scaled/log-domain products where needed; distinguish a true zero tensor map from floating-point underflow.
test: Check analytic uniform solutions at 150 and 400 members and nonuniform rankings on an asymmetric large uniform graph. Assert nonzero unit norm and honest convergence diagnostics.
resolution: Tensor directions use log-space products and stable normalization, including 150/400-node and asymmetric analytic controls.

title: Landscapes silently discard network weighting and concatenation
observed: A weighted transition network has A stay probability 1/3, but its landscape reports .4. A concat=3 network has stays A=2/3 and B=1/2, but its landscape reports .5 and 0. The discrepancy changes expected stays and depths. Landscape surfaces and trends use the same raw-sequence path.
cause: The landscape reads stored sequences and pools unweighted adjacent counts without replaying build_args/params. Weighting changes the estimand; concatenation also changes transitions and the bootstrap units. The API describes a landscape of the supplied transition network.
fix: Faithfully replay supported estimation settings, or explicitly reject models with unsupported settings and document the required raw-data estimand. Do not silently return another chain.
test: Assert full-length landscape stays agree with diag(network$weights) for weighted and concatenated fits, and verify bootstrap units/settings against an explicit reconstruction.
resolution: Landscapes replay weighting, concatenation and markers before counting; bootstrap units are merged sequences. Covariate conflicts and unrepresentable transformed chains produce informative errors. Surface stability measures retain every prepared position, including start markers.

title: A nonconstant measure can create a collapsed surface axis and crash
observed: With 21 valid sequences, 20 alternating A/B and one A/A/B/A, entropy varies but its 5th and 95th percentiles are both 1. landscape_surface() returns 25 copies of one slice; plot() fails with invalid y argument.
cause: Validation checks the full measure range, but the grid uses trimmed quantiles. Those endpoints can coincide for a discrete, strongly tied measure. Plotting deduplicates the values to one y coordinate, which persp() cannot render as a surface.
fix: Validate the actual grid endpoints; use a documented fallback range, a one-slice display, or a classed informative error. Avoid returning a nominal surface that its plot method cannot draw.
test: Test nonconstant measures whose trimmed quantiles coincide. Check both summary semantics and plot execution, alongside constant-measure and ordinary continuous-measure controls.
code:
s <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(c('A','B','A','B'),each=21),nrow=21))
s[21,] <- c('A','A','B','A')
a <- landscape_surface(s,k=5)
plot(a) # invalid y argument
resolution: Nonconstant measures and covariates with identical trimmed endpoints use their full range; both surface plots execute.

title: MOGen summaries overflow the new double-precision parameter counts
observed: A valid 10-state fit through order 10 stores finite path DOFs of 9e9 and 9e10 for its last two layers. summary() returns NA for those layer counts and produces integer-coercion warnings. Model criteria remain finite; this finding concerns summary output rather than invalid fitting.
cause: New path-based DOFs intentionally use doubles, but existing summary code casts them back to 32-bit integers. The new parameter-count representation was not propagated through the reporting API.
fix: Preserve numeric DOF columns in summaries and formatting. Check both layer and cumulative parameter counts.
test: Include a small valid fit with parameter counts above .Machine$integer.max; assert returned counts match stored values without warnings.
code:
set.seed(4)
s <- replicate(100,sample(LETTERS[1:10],14,TRUE),simplify=FALSE)
m <- build_mogen(s,max_order=10)
tail(m$layer_dof,2); tail(summary(m)$layer_dof,2)
resolution: MOGen summary preserves numeric layer/cumulative DOFs above the integer limit.

title: Small but nonconstant strengths normalize to NaN
observed: Public net_centrality() reports distinct incoming strengths of approximately 3e-12,1e-12,2e-12 but returns NaN for every normalized strength. The trigger involves extreme dwell/exit ratios and is lower priority than ordinary-input defects.
cause: The new constant-vector tolerance is 1e-10 times max(abs(endpoints),1). The unit floor imposes an absolute threshold and classifies substantial relative variation at a small scale as constant.
fix: Use a scale-sensitive tolerance and handle exact constant vectors separately. Preserve min-max normalization under positive common rescaling.
test: Test c(1,2,3) multiplied by several positive scales, plus exact-constant and rounding-noise vectors.
resolution: Scale-sensitive constant-vector detection preserves normalization of small, nonconstant values.

title: Literal stars-only states collide with pattern wildcard parsing
observed: Extraction accepts ** as a literal state. Unigram mining then raises an unclassed vapply error; bigram **→B receives lift .5 when its presence support .5 and state supports .5 and 1 imply lift 1.
cause: The pattern parser removes stars-only tokens regardless of whether they were observed state labels or inserted wildcard positions.
fix: Either reserve/reject stars-only labels with a documented classed error or keep wildcard positions structurally distinct from state labels.
test: Include ** and *** literals in unigram and bigram discovery, plus real gapped-pattern controls. Assert a correct result or a documented validation error.
resolution: Stars-only literal states are explicitly reserved and rejected with documented nestimate_bad_input; ordinary embedded stars remain valid.
